transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I suppose I'm just here because... I don't know, I just can't seem to sit still. Even when it's supposed to be a quiet day, I'm always up and moving. I'll start looking at the garden club list, and then before I know it I'm over by my knitting bag, and then I'm pulling out travel papers... I just never really finish any one thing before I'm on to the next.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually excited, overly energetic, or unusually confident, even to the point where others might have noticed a change in your behavior?
No... I don't think so. I wouldn't say I get unusually excited or... confident, or anything like that. I'm just restless, I suppose. Nobody has ever mentioned me acting strange.
Have you noticed any days where you feel a lack of interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, even your garden club or knitting?
No, not really. I mean... I still like those things. I just... don't always stick with them for very long at one time. But I still enjoy them.

Do you often find yourself acting quickly or making decisions without thinking them through, like interrupting others, spending money impulsively, or doing something without considering the consequences?

Well... I suppose I do interrupt sometimes. My husband mentions it. He says I cut him off before he's done talking. I don't mean to, it's just... if I don't say what I'm thinking right then, I'm afraid I'll forget it entirely. I guess I do it at the garden club planning meetings, too. I just... blurt things out.
Do you often find yourself struggling to finish tasks because your attention shifts easily to other things?
I suppose... yes. It doesn't take much. If someone's talking in the next room, or... if a car goes by the window, my mind just jumps right over there. And then I lose what I was doing. So, yes.
Do these difficulties with staying focused and interrupting happen in other places besides at home, like at the garden club meetings or when you're out running errands?

I suppose so... yes. It's... well, it's causing some strain, I guess. At home, and over at the community center. My husband and the other volunteers... they just can't really count on me to keep plans straight. Not without someone checking behind me, anyway.
Looking back, would you say these difficulties with focus and staying on task were noticeable when you were a child, maybe even as far back as elementary school?

I suppose... yes. It's been a long time, but... I think so. My mother used to say the teachers told her I was... bright, but scattered. Always losing my papers. And... I guess I talked out of turn even then, and couldn't sit still in my seat until my work was done. So... yes, I suppose it was noticeable back then.
